title: ThePrimeagen on Developer Excellence: bet on yourself, but pick the right problems
summary: ThePrimeagen's Laracon keynote tells how taking on a disliked Groovy backend at Netflix, with no connections and little seniority, led to a career that ended in streaming and YouTube. His core lesson is to bet on your ability to solve hard problems you don't yet know, but not at the cost of family or good judgment about what matters.

principles.text: Take the job nobody wants and do it as well as you can; it opens doors.
principles.quote: I just went in there and thought okay I could do this I can actually figure this out and I can do a really good job

principles.text: Betting you can solve something you don't yet know pays off for decades.
principles.quote: betting that you can solve something you do not know will pay not just dividends that year or the next year but for decades

principles.text: Determination and sustained effort can turn the worst student into the best, even without natural genius.
principles.quote: I'm going to do calculus I'm going to figure this kind of thing out

principles.text: Your drive for success must not cost you your relationships; extra grind hours don't decide startups.
principles.quote: an extra 10 hours has never made a startup succeed or fail ever

principles.text: Excellence needs both willingness to go the distance and judgment about which problems are worth solving.
principles.quote: intelligence is the ability to solve hard problems but wisdom is knowing which problems to solve

principles.text: Make content you genuinely love rather than chasing what you think everyone wants; it avoids burnout.
principles.quote: I'd rather try to do the things I want to do the way I want to do them than trying to figure out how to please just that one person
